title: China 1929-1936: Shanghai wholesale prices, the money supply, purchasing-power parity and real output (Brandt and Sargent 1989, Tables 1, 2, 4 and 5)
source: Loren Brandt and Thomas J. Sargent, 'Interpreting New Evidence about China and U.S. Silver Purchases', Journal of Monetary Economics 23 (1989) 31-51: Table 1 (wholesale prices, Shanghai, 1926 = 100; from T'ung-chi yue-pao, June 1937), Table 2 (money supply, year-end, million yuan; Rawski's estimates and the authors' revision), Table 4 (predicted and actual changes in wholesale prices) and Table 5 (sectoral output, billion 1933 yuan; K. C. Yeh)
series: year; shanghai_wpi_1926_100 (Table 1); silver_1a_myuan: monetary silver, column 1A; money_5a_myuan: Rawski's money supply, column 5A; money_6a_myuan: the revised money supply, column 6A (Table 2); gdp_bn_1933yuan and agriculture_bn_1933yuan (Table 5, 1931-1936); us_wpi_pct, usd_per_yuan_pct, predicted_shanghai_pct, actual_shanghai_pct: Table 4, columns 1-4, for the pair of years ending in 'year' (1930 = 1929/30): the percentage change of US wholesale prices, of the dollar price of the yuan, the predicted (1 - 2) and the actual change of Shanghai wholesale prices
